Activity Title: A1.1 — Emergency rehabilitation after flooding, August 2026 (corrected import)
Summary: Flooding damaged one water point and contaminated three; the team repaired the damaged hand pump, flushed and disinfected the three others, and the water quality officer retested them. Five thousand people regained safe water within a week.
Achievements: 3 water points rehabilitated and 4 retested after the floods; about 5,000 people with restored access.
Challenges: Floods in Jere and Konduga damaged one water point and contaminated three others, and about 400 households could not reach their latrines for a week. The water points were disinfected and retested, a flood contingency of hygiene kits was released and latrine access paths were raised.
Lessons Learned: Chlorinating and testing a water point at handover, before the community starts to use it, avoids early contamination complaints.
Next Steps: Complete the remaining water points and hand each over to its committee.

Summary: Each household received a hygiene kit (soap, bucket with lid, water treatment tablets and a leaflet) in Konduga town, Konduga LGA; households were selected from the community list with the committees and the distribution list was verified at the point of distribution.
Achievements: 1100 households received kits in August 2026; 1700 of 2,500 to date.
Challenges: Floods in Jere and Konduga damaged one water point and contaminated three others, and about 400 households could not reach their latrines for a week. The water points were disinfected and retested, a flood contingency of hygiene kits was released and latrine access paths were raised.
Lessons Learned: Distributing at the water point with a complaint desk reduces disputes about who is on the list.
Next Steps: Follow up use of the kits during the next hygiene sessions.

Activity Title: A2.3 — Post-flood water quality testing, August 2026 (corrected import)
Summary: The water quality officer tested 55 water points for free chlorine residual and, for a sample, bacteriology using portable test kits; 66 percent of the water points tested had a residual of at least 0.2 mg/l.
Achievements: 55 water quality tests carried out in August 2026; 290 of 320 to date. Chlorine compliance 66 percent.
Challenges: Floods in Jere and Konduga damaged one water point and contaminated three others, and about 400 households could not reach their latrines for a week. The water points were disinfected and retested, a flood contingency of hygiene kits was released and latrine access paths were raised.
Lessons Learned: A simple chlorinator at the water point and a weekly check by the committee raise compliance.
Next Steps: Retest the water points that failed and train committee members to read the kit.
